meta.disclaimer: General wellness information only. It is not a medical diagnosis or treatment plan. Check with a doctor before starting new exercise, yoga or diet changes, especially if you have a medical condition, are pregnant, or take medicines. Stop and seek help if you feel unwell.
meta.evidence_note: Compiled from commonly published public-health guidance (for example WHO physical-activity and healthy-diet recommendations, DASH-style diet principles, standard first-aid and home-care advice) and common yoga practice. Evidence labels are approximate. Review with a clinician, dietitian and certified yoga therapist before real-world use.

yoga.name: Tadasana (Mountain Pose)
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, weight even on both feet.
Lengthen the spine, relax the shoulders, arms by your sides.
Look straight ahead and breathe slowly through the nose.
Hold for 5 to 8 slow breaths, then relax.
yoga.benefits: Improves posture and body awareness; a calm start to a routine.
cautions: Sit down if you feel dizzy.
yoga.how_to: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, breathe slowly for 5-8 breaths.

yoga.name: Vrikshasana (Tree Pose)
steps: Stand near a wall or chair for support.
Shift weight to the left foot and rest the right foot on the left calf or ankle (never on the knee).
Bring palms together at the chest and look at a fixed point.
Hold for 5 breaths, then switch sides.
yoga.benefits: Improves balance and focus.
cautions: Keep a wall or chair within reach.
In pregnancy, keep the foot low and hold support.
yoga.how_to: Balance on one leg with the other foot on the calf, near a wall, 5 breaths per side.

yoga.name: Trikonasana (Triangle Pose)
steps: Stand with feet about one leg-length apart, right foot turned out.
Raise arms to shoulder height, then bend sideways over the right leg.
Rest the right hand on the shin or a block, left arm up. Look ahead or up if comfortable.
Hold for 3-5 breaths, come up slowly, switch sides.
yoga.benefits: Gently stretches the sides of the body, hips and legs.
cautions: Do not force the stretch.
Stop if you feel dizzy or have back pain.
yoga.how_to: Wide stance, bend sideways over one leg, hold 3-5 breaths each side.

yoga.name: Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose)
steps: Lie face down, palms under the shoulders, legs together.
Breathe in and lift the head and chest slightly, keeping the navel on the floor.
Keep elbows slightly bent and shoulders away from the ears.
Hold 3-5 breaths, lower slowly.
yoga.benefits: Strengthens the back muscles and opens the chest.
cautions: Keep the lift low. Avoid if you have abdominal surgery, hernia or acute back injury.
yoga.how_to: Lie on your belly, lift the chest low with elbows bent, 3-5 breaths.

yoga.name: Vajrasana (Thunderbolt Pose)
steps: Kneel and sit back on your heels, big toes touching.
Rest hands on the thighs, keep the spine upright.
Breathe normally. A folded blanket under the knees or between calves and thighs helps comfort.
yoga.benefits: A comfortable seated posture commonly used after meals to support digestion.
cautions: Come out if there is knee or ankle pain.
In pregnancy, sit on a cushion and do not press the belly.
yoga.how_to: Kneel and sit on your heels with a straight back for 5 minutes after meals.

yoga.name: Ardha Matsyendrasana (Half Spinal Twist)
steps: Sit with legs extended. Bend the right knee and place the foot outside the left thigh.
Breathe in and lengthen the spine, breathe out and twist to the right.
Keep the spine tall, do not pull with the arms.
Hold 5 breaths, release, repeat on the other side.
yoga.benefits: Improves spinal mobility and may help digestion.
cautions: Twist gently. Avoid with spinal injury, hernia or recent abdominal surgery.
yoga.how_to: Seated spinal twist, spine tall, 5 breaths each side.

yoga.name: Paschimottanasana (Seated Forward Bend)
steps: Sit with legs stretched forward, spine tall.
Breathe out and fold forward from the hips, reaching toward the shins or feet.
Keep knees slightly bent if the hamstrings are tight.
Hold 5-8 breaths, come up slowly.
yoga.benefits: Stretches the back and hamstrings and quiets the mind.
cautions: Never force the stretch. Avoid with sciatica or a disc problem.
yoga.how_to: Sit, fold forward from the hips with soft knees, 5-8 breaths.

yoga.name: Setu Bandhasana (Bridge Pose)
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet hip-width apart near the hips.
Press the feet down and lift the hips, keeping the neck relaxed.
Hold 3-5 breaths and lower the spine slowly.
yoga.benefits: Strengthens the back, glutes and legs; opens the chest.
cautions: Do not turn the head while lifted. Avoid with neck injury.
yoga.how_to: Lie on your back, lift the hips for 3-5 breaths, lower slowly.

yoga.name: Marjaryasana-Bitilasana (Cat-Cow)
steps: Come onto hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
Breathe in: drop the belly and lift the chest and tailbone (cow).
Breathe out: round the back and tuck the chin (cat).
Move slowly with the breath for 8-10 rounds.
yoga.benefits: Gently mobilises the spine and eases stiffness from sitting.
cautions: Pad the knees. Move within a comfortable range.
yoga.how_to: On hands and knees, arch and round the back slowly with the breath, 8-10 rounds.

yoga.name: Balasana (Child's Pose)
steps: Kneel, big toes together, knees apart (wide, if pregnant).
Sit back toward the heels and fold forward, resting the forehead on the floor or a cushion.
Arms stretched forward or beside the body. Breathe slowly into the back.
yoga.benefits: A restful posture that eases back tension and calms the mind.
cautions: Place a cushion under the knees or hips if uncomfortable.
yoga.how_to: Kneel, fold forward and rest the forehead down, breathing slowly for 1-3 minutes.

yoga.name: Pawanmuktasana (Wind-Relieving Pose)
steps: Lie on your back. Bend the right knee and hug it toward the chest.
Breathe slowly and hold for 5 breaths, then switch legs.
Finally hug both knees together for 5 breaths.
yoga.benefits: Helps relieve gas and bloating.
cautions: Avoid after meals. Skip if you have a hernia or recent abdominal surgery.
yoga.how_to: Lie on your back, hug one knee then both knees to the chest for 5 breaths each.

yoga.name: Shavasana (Relaxation Pose)
steps: Lie on your back, legs slightly apart, arms relaxed with palms up.
Close the eyes and let the breath become slow and natural.
Relax the body part by part, from feet to head.
Stay for 5-10 minutes, then roll to one side before sitting up slowly.
yoga.frequency: daily, after exercise or before bed
yoga.benefits: Deep rest that supports stress and blood pressure management.
cautions: In pregnancy, lie on the left side with a pillow between the knees.
yoga.how_to: Lie still, breathe naturally and relax each body part for 5-10 minutes.

yoga.name: Viparita Karani (Legs-Up-the-Wall)
steps: Sit sideways next to a wall and swing the legs up as you lie back.
Keep the hips close to the wall, arms relaxed.
Breathe slowly for 5 minutes, then bend the knees and roll to the side.
yoga.benefits: A restful pose commonly used for tired legs and winding down.
cautions: Skip if you have high blood pressure, glaucoma or heart disease.
yoga.how_to: Lie with legs up the wall for 5 minutes (not for high BP or glaucoma).

yoga.name: Sukhasana (Easy Pose)
steps: Sit cross-legged on a folded blanket so the hips are above the knees.
Keep the spine tall, hands on the knees.
Breathe slowly and stay for several minutes.
yoga.benefits: A comfortable base posture for breathing and meditation.
cautions: Change the crossing of the legs from time to time.
yoga.how_to: Sit cross-legged on a cushion with a tall spine and breathe slowly.

yoga.name: Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation, slow pace)
steps: Start standing in prayer pose.
Move slowly through the 12 positions, matching breath to movement.
Begin with 2-3 rounds and build up gradually.
Finish with Shavasana for 3-5 minutes.
yoga.benefits: Whole-body movement that raises the heart rate gently.
cautions: Not for high blood pressure, heart disease, pregnancy or back problems. Learn from a trained teacher.
yoga.how_to: 12-step flowing sequence, 2-3 slow rounds (not for high BP, heart disease or pregnancy).

yoga.name: Ardha Kati Chakrasana (Standing Side Bend)
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, right arm up.
Bend gently to the left, keeping both hips facing forward.
Hold 3-5 breaths, return to centre, switch sides.
yoga.benefits: Stretches the sides of the trunk and loosens the spine.
cautions: Do not lean forward or back.
yoga.how_to: Stand, raise one arm and bend sideways for 3-5 breaths each side.

yoga.name: Neck and Shoulder Release
steps: Sit tall. Slowly drop the right ear toward the right shoulder, hold 5 breaths, switch.
Roll the shoulders backward 10 times, then forward 10 times.
Gently turn the head left and right, only as far as comfortable.
yoga.benefits: Eases tension from long sitting or screen use.
cautions: No fast or full neck circles. Stop if you feel dizzy or have arm tingling.
yoga.how_to: Slow ear-to-shoulder stretches and shoulder rolls every couple of hours.

yoga.name: Chair Yoga Flow
steps: Sit tall on a sturdy chair, feet flat.
Do seated side bends, gentle twists and cat-cow with hands on the knees, 5 each.
Lift and lower the arms with the breath 8 times.
Finish with 5 slow deep breaths.
yoga.benefits: Mobility and gentle movement for people who find floor poses hard.
cautions: Use a chair without wheels.
yoga.how_to: Seated side bends, twists and arm raises with slow breathing.

yoga.name: Deep Abdominal (Diaphragmatic) Breathing
steps: Sit or lie comfortably with one hand on the belly.
Breathe in slowly through the nose for about 4 counts so the belly rises.
Breathe out slowly for about 6 counts so the belly falls.
Continue for 5-10 minutes without strain.
yoga.benefits: Slow breathing is linked with lower stress and modest blood pressure reduction.
cautions: Stop and breathe normally if you feel light-headed.
yoga.how_to: Slow belly breathing: in for 4, out for 6, for 5-10 minutes.

yoga.name: Anulom Vilom (Alternate Nostril Breathing, no breath-holding)
steps: Sit tall. Close the right nostril with the thumb and breathe in through the left.
Close the left nostril with the ring finger and breathe out through the right.
Breathe in through the right, out through the left. This is one round.
Do 5-10 rounds at an easy pace. Do not hold the breath.
yoga.benefits: Calming breathing practice used for stress and relaxation.
cautions: Do NOT hold the breath if you have high blood pressure, heart disease or are pregnant.
Skip if your nose is blocked.
yoga.how_to: Alternate nostril breathing without holding the breath, 5-10 rounds.

yoga.name: Bhramari (Humming Bee Breath)
steps: Sit comfortably, close the eyes.
Breathe in through the nose, then breathe out slowly while making a soft humming sound.
Feel the vibration around the head and face.
Repeat 5-8 times.
yoga.benefits: The humming and slow exhale have a calming effect.
cautions: Keep the hum gentle. Avoid with an ear infection.
yoga.how_to: Soft humming on a slow exhale, 5-8 rounds.

yoga.name: Yoga Nidra (Guided Relaxation)
steps: Lie down comfortably (on the left side if pregnant) and close your eyes.
Follow a guided recording that moves attention through the body.
Let the breath be natural; stay awake but deeply relaxed.
Come out slowly by moving fingers and toes.
yoga.benefits: Guided deep relaxation that can help sleep and stress.
cautions: Use a calm guided recording.
yoga.how_to: Lie down and follow a guided body-scan relaxation for 15-25 minutes.

yoga.name: Mindful Breathing Meditation
steps: Sit comfortably with a straight back.
Place attention on the breath at the nostrils or belly.
When the mind wanders, notice it and return to the breath.
Start with 5 minutes and slowly increase.
yoga.benefits: Helps manage stress and supports better sleep.
cautions: If it makes you anxious, stop and talk to a health worker.
yoga.how_to: Watch the breath for 5-15 minutes and gently return when the mind wanders.

practices_to_avoid.name: Kapalabhati and Bhastrika (forceful breathing)
practices_to_avoid.why: Fast forceful breathing can raise blood pressure and strain the abdomen.

practices_to_avoid.name: Breath retention (kumbhaka)
practices_to_avoid.why: Holding the breath can raise blood pressure and heart workload.

practices_to_avoid.name: Headstand (Sirsasana) and Shoulder stand (Sarvangasana)
practices_to_avoid.why: Inversions raise pressure in the head and load the neck. Learn only from a qualified teacher.

practices_to_avoid.name: Deep backbends such as Dhanurasana
practices_to_avoid.why: Deep backbends compress the spine and abdomen.

practices_to_avoid.name: Hot yoga or practising in extreme heat
practices_to_avoid.why: Heat adds to dehydration and heart strain.

exercise.name: Brisk Walking
exercise.intensity: moderate (you can talk but not sing)
steps: Warm up with 3-5 minutes of easy walking.
Walk at a pace where you breathe faster but can still talk.
Cool down with 3-5 minutes of slow walking and light stretching.
Build up by 5 minutes a week if you are new to exercise.
exercise.benefits: Supports heart health, blood pressure, blood sugar and weight; improves mood.
cautions: Wear comfortable shoes. Avoid peak afternoon heat; carry water.
exercise.how_to: 30 minutes of brisk walking, 5 days a week.

exercise.name: Short Walk After Meals
steps: Start walking 10-15 minutes after you finish eating.
Keep an easy, steady pace.
exercise.benefits: A short walk after eating helps lower the blood sugar rise after meals.
cautions: Do not start with heavy exercise right after a meal.
exercise.how_to: Walk gently for 10-15 minutes after meals.

exercise.name: Cycling or Stationary Bike
steps: Set the seat so the knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Pedal at a steady, comfortable pace.
Cool down with 3 minutes of easy pedalling.
exercise.benefits: Low-impact aerobic exercise that is kind to the knees.
cautions: Use a stationary bike if road traffic or heat is a concern. In pregnancy, prefer a stationary bike.
exercise.how_to: 20-30 minutes of steady cycling, 3-5 days a week.

exercise.name: Swimming or Water Walking
steps: Warm up with slow laps or walking in chest-deep water.
Swim or walk at a steady pace.
Cool down and stretch.
exercise.benefits: Full-body exercise with very little joint stress.
cautions: Swim only where there is a lifeguard or trained supervision.
exercise.how_to: 20-30 minutes of swimming or water walking, 2-3 days a week.

exercise.name: Simple Strength Exercises
steps: Sit-to-stand from a chair: 8-12 repeats.
Wall push-ups: 8-12 repeats.
Step-ups on a low step: 8-10 per leg.
Do 2 rounds, resting 1 minute between exercises.
exercise.benefits: Builds muscle and bone strength and helps blood sugar control.
cautions: Breathe out as you push or stand; never hold your breath.
exercise.how_to: Sit-to-stand, wall push-ups and step-ups, 2-3 days a week.

exercise.name: Resistance Band Exercises
steps: Seated rows with the band: 10 repeats.
Band arm press: 10 repeats.
Band leg press while seated: 10 repeats per leg.
Rest between sets.
exercise.benefits: Safe strength work for older adults and beginners.
cautions: Check the band for tears before use.
exercise.how_to: Gentle seated band exercises, 2-3 days a week.

exercise.name: Desk Break Stretches
steps: Stand up and walk for 1-2 minutes.
Reach both arms overhead and stretch tall.
Gentle neck side stretches and shoulder rolls.
Stretch the chest by clasping hands behind the back.
exercise.benefits: Breaks up long sitting and eases neck, shoulder and back tension.
cautions: Avoid fast neck circles.
stop_if: numbness or tingling in the arm
exercise.how_to: Stand, walk and stretch for 3-5 minutes every hour.

exercise.name: Pelvic Floor (Kegel) Exercises
steps: Tighten the muscles you would use to stop passing urine, without using the belly or thighs.
Hold for 3-5 seconds and relax for 5 seconds.
Do 8-10 repeats, 2-3 times a day.
exercise.benefits: Supports bladder control and recovery around pregnancy and childbirth.
cautions: After delivery, start only when your doctor or midwife says it is fine.
exercise.how_to: Squeeze and hold the pelvic floor 3-5 seconds, 8-10 repeats, 2-3 times a day.

exercise.name: Balance Exercises
steps: Stand next to a wall or counter for support.
Stand on one leg for 10-20 seconds, then switch.
Walk heel-to-toe along a line for 10 steps.
Repeat 2-3 times.
exercise.benefits: Helps prevent falls in older adults.
cautions: Always keep something sturdy within reach.
exercise.how_to: Single-leg standing and heel-to-toe walking near a support, 3 days a week.

exercise.name: Low-Impact Marching and Step Routine
steps: March on the spot, lifting the knees to a comfortable height.
Add gentle arm swings.
Alternate 2 minutes of marching with 1 minute of rest.
Repeat 5-6 times.
exercise.benefits: Indoor activity that is easy on the joints.
cautions: Hold a chair for balance if needed.
exercise.how_to: March on the spot for 2 minutes, rest 1 minute, repeat 5-6 times.

exercise.name: Gentle Walking in Pregnancy
steps: Walk at a comfortable pace on flat ground.
Carry water and walk in the cooler part of the day.
Stop and rest when tired.
exercise.benefits: Helps energy, mood, sleep and healthy weight gain in pregnancy.
cautions: Only if your doctor has not advised rest. Stop for bleeding, leaking fluid, dizziness or pain.
exercise.how_to: 20-30 minutes of easy walking on most days (if your doctor agrees).

exercise.name: Active Play for Children and Teenagers
steps: Encourage running, cycling, skipping, football, kabaddi or swimming.
Limit screen time and break up sitting with movement.
Include bone-strengthening play such as jumping a few times a week.
exercise.benefits: Children and teenagers (5-17 years) are advised about 60 minutes of physical activity a day.
cautions: Keep children hydrated; avoid the hottest hours.
exercise.how_to: About 60 minutes of active play every day.

exercise.name: Activity Plan for Older Adults (60+)
steps: Combine easy walking, light strength work and balance exercises across the week.
Add balance work on at least 3 days.
Move a little every day, even if only for short stretches.
exercise.benefits: A mix of walking, strength and balance supports independence and lowers the risk of falls.
cautions: Start slowly and increase gradually. Talk to your doctor if you have heart or joint problems.
exercise.how_to: Walking, light strength and balance work through the week.

do: Aim for at least 400 g (about 5 portions) of vegetables and fruit a day.
Choose whole grains such as whole wheat roti, brown rice, millets and oats.
Include a protein source at most meals: dal, legumes, curd, paneer, eggs, fish or chicken.
Drink water regularly through the day (clear or pale urine is a good sign).
limit: Keep salt under 5 g (about 1 teaspoon) a day in total.
Limit sugary drinks, sweets, and packaged or deep-fried snacks.
Limit free sugars to under 10% of daily energy.

sample_day.breakfast: Vegetable upma or poha with a glass of buttermilk
sample_day.lunch: 2 rotis, dal, mixed vegetables, salad, curd
sample_day.dinner: Light khichdi with vegetables or 1-2 rotis with sabzi

diet.notes: Based on commonly published healthy-diet guidance. Adjust to local foods, culture and food allergies.

do: Cut salt at the table and in cooking; use lemon, herbs, jeera and ginger for flavour.
Eat more potassium-rich foods: banana, coconut water, leafy greens, beans, tomatoes (unless your doctor restricts potassium).
Choose whole grains, vegetables, fruit and low-fat dairy.
Prefer fresh home-cooked food over packaged and canned food.
limit: Avoid pickles, papad, salted snacks (namkeen), processed meats and instant noodles.
Limit alcohol and avoid smoking and chewing tobacco.
Limit tea and coffee if they make your heart race.
indian_examples: moong dal khichdi with little salt

sample_day.breakfast: Oats or vegetable daliya with low salt and a banana
sample_day.lunch: 2 rotis, dal (low salt), green vegetables, cucumber-tomato salad, curd

diet.notes: Reducing salt and eating more fruit and vegetables is among the best-supported diet advice for blood pressure. If you take BP medicines or kidney medicines, ask your doctor about potassium and salt substitutes.
tips: Cut salt at the table and in cooking; use lemon, herbs, jeera and ginger for flavour.
Eat more potassium-rich foods: banana, coconut water, leafy greens, beans, tomatoes (unless your doctor restricts potassium).
Choose whole grains, vegetables, fruit and low-fat dairy.
Prefer fresh home-cooked food over packaged and canned food.

diet.focus: Blood sugar friendly eating (low glycaemic index)
do: Choose whole grains and millets (ragi, jowar, bajra) in place of refined flour (maida) and polished white rice.
Fill half the plate with non-starchy vegetables and add dal, legumes or other protein.
Eat at regular times; do not skip meals.
Choose whole fruit (such as guava, apple, papaya) in sensible portions instead of juice.
limit: Avoid sugary drinks, sweets, mithai and sweetened tea or coffee.
Keep portions of white rice, potatoes and bread modest.
Limit fried snacks and bakery items.
indian_examples: bitter gourd or bottle gourd sabzi

sample_day.breakfast: Besan chilla or vegetable oats with curd
sample_day.lunch: 1-2 millet rotis, dal, large portion of sabzi, salad
sample_day.snack: A handful of roasted chana or nuts
sample_day.dinner: Vegetable soup, paneer or egg bhurji with 1 roti

diet.notes: If you take diabetes medicines or insulin, check your sugar as advised and do not change doses without your doctor. High readings need a proper test and medical advice.
tips: Choose whole grains and millets (ragi, jowar, bajra) in place of refined flour (maida) and polished white rice.
Fill half the plate with non-starchy vegetables and add dal, legumes or other protein.

do: Use small amounts of unsaturated oils (mustard, groundnut, sunflower, olive) and rotate oils.
Add fibre: oats, whole pulses, vegetables, fruit.
Eat a small handful of nuts (almonds, walnuts) most days.
If you eat fish, include it about twice a week.
limit: Avoid trans fats (vanaspati, many bakery and packaged fried foods).
Limit ghee, butter, cream and fried foods.
Limit red and processed meat.

sample_day.breakfast: Oats with fruit and nuts, or idli with sambar
sample_day.lunch: Brown rice or roti, dal, vegetables, salad
sample_day.dinner: Grilled fish or paneer tikka with vegetables, 1 roti

diet.notes: Diet is one part of heart care. Treatment of high cholesterol, blood pressure and diabetes needs a doctor.
tips: Use small amounts of unsaturated oils (mustard, groundnut, sunflower, olive) and rotate oils.
Add fibre: oats, whole pulses, vegetables, fruit.
Eat a small handful of nuts (almonds, walnuts) most days.
If you eat fish, include it about twice a week.

do: Use smaller plates and fill half of the plate with vegetables.
Eat slowly and stop when you feel comfortably full.
Choose protein and fibre-rich foods to feel full for longer.
Aim for gradual weight loss (for example about 0.25-0.5 kg a week) rather than crash diets.
limit: Avoid sugary drinks and frequent fried or packaged snacks.
Avoid skipping meals and then overeating.
Do not use crash diets or unproven weight-loss supplements.

sample_day.breakfast: Moong dal chilla with mint chutney
sample_day.lunch: 1-2 rotis, dal, large serving of vegetables, salad
sample_day.dinner: Vegetable soup and grilled paneer, chicken or tofu with salad

diet.notes: For Asian adults, a BMI of 23 or more already raises health risk. Ask a doctor or dietitian for a personal plan.
tips: Use smaller plates and fill half of the plate with vegetables.
Eat slowly and stop when you feel comfortably full.
Choose protein and fibre-rich foods to feel full for longer.

do: Eat 3 meals and 2-3 snacks a day.
Add nutritious energy: nuts, nut butter, milk, curd, eggs, paneer, ghee in small amounts.
Include protein with every meal.
Pair meals with light activity to build appetite and muscle.
limit: Avoid filling up on tea, coffee or empty-calorie snacks before meals.

sample_day.breakfast: Paneer or egg paratha with milk
sample_day.lunch: Rice or roti, dal, vegetables, curd
sample_day.snack: Banana shake or a handful of nuts
sample_day.dinner: Khichdi with ghee, vegetables and curd

diet.notes: Persistent weight loss or a low BMI should be checked by a doctor to rule out an illness.

do: Eat smaller, more frequent meals.
Finish dinner at least 2-3 hours before lying down.
Raise the head of the bed slightly if heartburn happens at night.
Notice and avoid your own trigger foods.
limit: Limit very spicy, oily or fried foods, strong tea or coffee on an empty stomach, and carbonated drinks.
Avoid smoking and alcohol.
indian_examples: cold milk or curd if it suits you

sample_day.lunch: Roti, dal, boiled or lightly cooked vegetables
sample_day.snack: Fruit or a glass of cold milk
sample_day.dinner: Early, light meal such as khichdi or vegetable soup

diet.notes: See a doctor if heartburn is frequent, wakes you at night, or comes with vomiting, black stools, weight loss or trouble swallowing.
tips: Eat smaller, more frequent meals.

Notice and avoid your own trigger foods.

do: Increase fibre slowly: vegetables, fruit with skin, whole grains, pulses.
Drink enough water through the day.
Eat at regular times and do not ignore the urge to go.
Move daily; even a walk helps.

diet.focus: Soothing a mild cold or cough
do: Rest and drink warm fluids often (warm water, soups, ginger-tulsi tea).
Gargle with warm salt water for a sore throat.
Adults and children over 1 year can take a spoon of honey for a cough.
Eat light, easy-to-digest food.
limit: Do not give honey to babies under 1 year.
Avoid smoking and smoke exposure.
Avoid cold drinks if they worsen the throat.

sample_day.lunch: Dal, rice or roti, cooked vegetables

diet.notes: See a doctor if there is fever for more than 3 days, trouble breathing, chest pain, or the cough lasts over 2 weeks.
tips: Rest and drink warm fluids often (warm water, soups, ginger-tulsi tea).
Gargle with warm salt water for a sore throat.
Adults and children over 1 year can take a spoon of honey for a cough.

do: Take oral rehydration solution (ORS) in small, frequent sips.
Keep eating light foods: rice, banana, curd, khichdi.
Wash hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.
Drink only safe, boiled or filtered water.
limit: Avoid sugary drinks and very oily food.
Do not take antibiotics or anti-diarrhoeal medicines without medical advice.
diet.notes: Go to a health centre urgently for blood in stool, very frequent watery stools, vomiting that stops fluids, sunken eyes, very dry mouth, or a child who is very sleepy or cannot drink. Babies and young children can dehydrate fast.
tips: Take oral rehydration solution (ORS) in small, frequent sips.
Keep eating light foods: rice, banana, curd, khichdi.
Wash hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.

do: Eat regular, balanced meals with extra protein: dal, milk, curd, eggs, paneer, legumes.
Include iron- and folate-rich foods: leafy greens, beans, jaggery in small amounts, fruit.
Take iron and folic acid tablets and any supplements exactly as prescribed.
Drink plenty of safe water and eat small, frequent meals if nauseous.
limit: Avoid alcohol, tobacco and raw or undercooked meat, fish and eggs.
Avoid unpasteurised milk and cheese.
Limit tea and coffee (caffeine).

Rest when the baby sleeps.
limit: Avoid alcohol and smoking.
Do not follow extreme restrictions or crash diets.

do: Eat small, frequent, nutritious meals.
Include enough protein (dal, milk, curd, eggs, fish, paneer).
Include calcium (milk, curd, ragi, leafy greens) and get safe morning sunlight for vitamin D.
Drink water regularly even if you do not feel thirsty.
limit: Limit salt and sugar.
Avoid very hard or hard-to-chew foods if chewing is difficult.

sample_day.lunch: Roti or rice, dal, soft cooked vegetables, curd

do: Breastfeed exclusively for the first 6 months, then continue with safe, age-appropriate complementary foods.
Offer a variety of foods: dal, vegetables, fruit, milk, eggs and grains.
Offer regular meals and healthy snacks.
Encourage safe water and handwashing before meals.
limit: Avoid sugary drinks, chips and packaged snacks.
Do not give honey to babies under 1 year.
Avoid whole nuts to young children (choking risk).

do: Drink water regularly through the day, before you feel thirsty.
Take ORS, lemon water with a pinch of salt and sugar, buttermilk or coconut water in heat.
Wear light clothing and stay in the shade during peak heat.
Eat fruits with high water content such as watermelon and cucumber.
limit: Avoid strenuous work outdoors in the hottest hours.
Limit alcohol and very sugary drinks.

lifestyle.title: Good sleep habits
tips: Adults: aim for 7-9 hours; school-age children need more.
Keep a regular sleep and wake time, even on holidays.
Switch off phones and TV 30-60 minutes before bed.
Keep the bedroom dark, quiet and cool.
Avoid tea, coffee and heavy meals late in the evening.
lifestyle.why: Poor sleep is linked with higher blood pressure, blood sugar and stress.

lifestyle.title: Managing stress
tips: Take short breathing breaks during the day.
Talk to someone you trust about worries.
Spend time on hobbies, prayer, music or time outdoors.
Break big tasks into small steps.
Seek help from a counsellor or doctor if worry or low mood lasts for weeks.
lifestyle.why: Long-term stress affects sleep, blood pressure and mood.

lifestyle.title: Checking blood pressure at home
tips: Rest for 5 minutes, sit with back supported and feet flat; arm at heart level.
Avoid tea, coffee, smoking and exercise for 30 minutes before checking.
Take 2 readings one minute apart and write them down with the date.
Take the log to your doctor.
lifestyle.why: Home readings help your doctor decide on treatment.

lifestyle.title: Stop tobacco and cut down alcohol
tips: Any form of tobacco, including chewing tobacco, harms the heart and lungs; quitting helps at any age.
Ask a health worker or doctor about quit support.
If you drink alcohol, keep it low or avoid it, especially with high blood pressure.
lifestyle.why: Tobacco and alcohol raise the risk of heart disease, stroke and cancer.

lifestyle.title: Looking after your feet
tips: Check your feet every day for cuts, blisters, redness or swelling.
Wash and dry between the toes; moisturise dry skin but not between the toes.
Wear comfortable, well-fitting footwear and avoid walking barefoot.
Get any wound or sore checked early.
lifestyle.why: High blood sugar can reduce feeling in the feet so small injuries go unnoticed.

lifestyle.title: Regular health check-ups
tips: Have your blood pressure checked at least once a year, more often if it is high.
Adults should have a blood sugar check regularly, especially with family history or extra weight.
Keep your vaccinations up to date.
Ask your doctor about cholesterol and other screening for your age.

lifestyle.title: Healthy posture and screen use
tips: Sit with back supported, feet flat and screen at eye level.
Stand and move for a few minutes every hour.
Follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Lift objects by bending the knees, not the back.
lifestyle.why: Poor posture and long sitting contribute to neck, back and eye strain.

lifestyle.title: Hand hygiene and infection prevention
tips: Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, especially before eating and after the toilet.
Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or elbow.
Stay home and rest when you have a fever or bad cold.
Keep vaccinations up to date.
lifestyle.why: Handwashing reduces many infections including diarrhoea and respiratory illness.

lifestyle.title: Safe sunlight
tips: Get about 10-20 minutes of morning sunlight on the arms and face when convenient, avoiding peak midday sun.
Ask your doctor whether you need a vitamin D supplement.
lifestyle.why: Sunlight helps the body make vitamin D for bones and muscles.

lifestyle.title: Heat safety
tips: Avoid outdoor work and exercise in the hottest hours (about 12 to 4 pm).
Wear light, loose, light-coloured clothing and cover the head.
Never leave children or pets in a parked vehicle.
Drink water or ORS regularly.
lifestyle.why: Heat illness can become serious quickly.

lifestyle.title: Mental well-being
tips: Keep in touch with family and friends.
Do something you enjoy every day.
Do not suffer in silence: speak to a doctor or counsellor if you feel hopeless, very anxious or unable to cope.
lifestyle.why: Mental health is part of overall health, and help is available.

lifestyle.title: Antenatal care essentials
tips: Attend all antenatal check-ups and scans advised.
Take iron, folic acid and calcium as prescribed.
Rest on your left side when lying down in later pregnancy.
Know the danger signs: bleeding, severe headache, blurred vision, severe swelling, reduced baby movements, fits, fever or leaking fluid. Go to a hospital at once.
lifestyle.why: Regular care and knowing danger signs save lives of mothers and babies.

lifestyle.title: Preventing falls at home
tips: Keep floors dry and free of loose rugs and clutter.
Use night lights and handrails in the bathroom and stairs.
Wear well-fitting non-slip footwear.
Stand up slowly from bed or chair.
lifestyle.why: Falls are a major cause of injury in older adults.

lifestyle.title: Tracking weight and waist
tips: Weigh yourself about once a week at the same time and write it down.
Keep a simple food and walking diary for 2 weeks to spot habits.
Set small goals such as an extra 1,000 steps a day.
lifestyle.why: Tracking helps you see progress and stay motivated.

lifestyle.title: If you are underweight
tips: Eat regularly with protein at each meal.
Add gentle strength exercise to build muscle.
See a doctor if weight keeps falling without a reason.
lifestyle.why: A low BMI can be linked to poor nutrition or illness.

home_care: Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids.
Salt-water gargles may soothe the throat.
Wash hands often and cover coughs.
avoid: Do not take antibiotics unless a doctor prescribes them.
see_doctor_if: A baby under 3 months has any fever

home_care: Warm fluids; honey in warm water for adults and children over 1 year.
Rest and avoid smoke.
Sit upright to sleep with an extra pillow.
avoid: Do not give honey to babies under 1 year.
Avoid cough syrups in young children unless advised by a doctor.

home_care: Warm salt-water gargles several times a day.
Warm fluids and rest.
Avoid very cold drinks if they irritate.
Drink water, rest in a quiet place and relax the neck and shoulders.
Take a short walk or do gentle neck stretches.
Limit screen time and check that you are sleeping enough.
see_doctor_if: Sudden severe headache or the worst of your life
Headache with fever and stiff neck
Weakness, confusion, vision or speech changes

home_care: Eat smaller meals and avoid lying down for 2-3 hours after eating.
Cut back on spicy, oily food and strong tea or coffee.
Raise the head of the bed slightly.
see_doctor_if: Chest pain, especially with sweating or breathlessness (seek emergency care)
Heartburn more than twice a week

home_care: More fibre (vegetables, fruit, whole grains) and water.
Walk daily and go to the toilet at a regular time.
Do not ignore the urge to go.
avoid: Avoid frequent laxative use without advice.

home_care: Rest the area for a day, then resume gentle movement.
Warm compress or a warm bath for stiffness; a cold pack for a fresh swelling.
Gentle stretching once the pain eases.
avoid: Avoid heavy lifting until the pain settles.
see_doctor_if: Pain after a fall or injury
Loss of bladder or bowel control
Pain that wakes you at night or lasts more than 2 weeks

home_care: Wash hands, then rinse the wound under clean running water and wash gently with soap.
Press with a clean cloth to stop bleeding.
Cover with a clean dressing and change daily.
avoid: Do not apply turmeric, ash, toothpaste or other home powders on an open wound.
see_doctor_if: Bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of pressure
The cut is deep, gaping or dirty
Signs of infection: spreading redness, warmth, pus, fever
You are not up to date with tetanus vaccination

home_care: Wash with soap and water; apply a cold cloth.
Avoid scratching to prevent infection.
A mild calamine lotion can ease itching.
see_doctor_if: Swelling of the face, lips or tongue or trouble breathing (emergency)

home_care: Keep a regular sleep schedule and aim for 7-9 hours.
Get daylight and light activity during the day.
Avoid caffeine in the evening.
avoid: Avoid sleeping pills without a doctor's advice.
see_doctor_if: Low mood or loss of interest

home_care: Take ORS in small, frequent sips.
Continue light food such as rice, banana, curd and khichdi.
Wash hands with soap; drink safe water.
avoid: Do not take antibiotics or anti-diarrhoeal medicines without advice.
see_doctor_if: Signs of dehydration: very dry mouth, sunken eyes, very little urine, extreme sleepiness
Vomiting so that fluids cannot be kept down
Lasts more than 2 days, or any diarrhoea in a young baby

when_to_seek_care: Chest pain or pressure, or severe trouble breathing: call 108 / 112 now.
Fainting, confusion, a fit (seizure) or sudden weakness or numbness on one side.
Sudden severe headache, face drooping or slurred speech.
Heavy bleeding that does not stop, or vomiting blood.
Signs of severe allergy: swelling of the lips or tongue, trouble breathing.
A pregnant woman with bleeding, severe headache, blurred vision, fits, or reduced baby movements.
A child who cannot drink or breastfeed, is very sleepy or hard to wake, has a fit or fast breathing.
